title: Introduce segment-mapper & vocab-bridge to rationalize model bootstrap and lazy weight activation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: the model bootstrap path currently contains a tangle of format-specific deserializers and tokenizer-vocab assumptions. Different checkpoints ('.pt', 'safetensors', 'gguf') and sharding schemes (contiguous, interleaved, per-layer-split) are handled by ad-hoc loaders. Tokenizer/vocab formats are sometimes embedded in checkpoint metadata which forces early tokenizer instantiation and prevents lazy weight activation. This leads to long cold-start times, high peak memory during load, duplicated deserialization logic, and brittle upgrades when we add new formats or sharding strategies.

Proposal: implement two cooperating abstractions: (1) segment-mapper - a deterministic mapping layer that translates checkpoint segments and shard descriptors into canonical runtime segments (tensor id + byte range + shape + dtype), and (2) vocab-bridge - a thin compatibility layer that canonicalizes tokenizer/vocab representations into a runtime token-id map without forcing tokenizer construction during weight hydrate. Together with a lazy weight-activation step (on-demand tensor materialization + zero-copy mmap where possible), these will: reduce peak memory, shorten model bootstrap wall time, and centralize format negotiation logic.

Scope/Deliverables:
- Segment-mapper core library with format adapters for .pt, safetensors, gguf and the three known sharding styles. Adapter interface defined and documented.
- Vocab-bridge that accepts multiple tokenizer artifacts (BPE merges/vocab.json, SentencePiece .model, gguf vocab block) and exposes a canonical token->id table and optional vocab fingerprint.
- Lazy weight activation runtime: manifest-driven loader that allocates tensor placeholders and materializes data on first use; supports mmap/zero-copy for read-only artifacts and background async deserialization for non-mmap-friendly formats.
- Compatibility shim: a find-first fallback that allows old checkpoints to be loaded unchanged; opt-in flag to enable strict mapping for new checkpoints.
- End-to-end tests and rollout plan: unit tests per adapter, integration tests with small models, performance benchmark harness comparing current baseline vs segment-mapper path.

Trade-offs & decisions so far:
- We will not rewrite all existing checkpoint writers. Instead implement adapters that read current formats at load-time (adapter-per-format). Writers can be consolidated later.
- Eager tokenizer initialization will be preserved behind a feature flag during rollout to guard downstream integrations that assume tokenizer ready on bootstrap.
- Using mmap as preferred pathway reduces CPU deserialization but requires an owner policy for ephemeral dirty pages; we'll rely on existing eviction heuristics in the runtime.

Progress so far:
- Inventory completed: sampled top-50 customer checkpoints, captured format variants and sharding patterns. (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Model+Format+Inventory)
- Design doc drafted and reviewed by infra and applied-ml. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Segment+Mapper+Design
- PoC segment-mapper for safetensors + contiguous-shard implemented; local integration shows ~22% lower peak RSS on load for a 7B model. PoC branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284

Next steps (this cycle):
- Land format-adapters for .pt and gguf (Diego)
- Implement vocab-bridge and its canonical token table (Maya)
- Add integration test harness that measures peak RSS, wall-time, and mmap vs deserialize paths (SRE/Bench)
- Prepare a canary rollout plan for runtime-1.21 with feature-flag gating and telemetry hooks (product + reliability)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: subtle token-id mismatches during migration. Mitigation: generate token mapping diffs and compare top-100k token ids across legacy vs vocab-bridge; if diff > threshold, block rollout for that model family.
- Risk: mmap not available in some on-prem deployments (air-gapped). Mitigation: runtime falls back to streaming deserialization path; document performance implications.

Acceptance criteria:
- Segment-mapper exposes stable adapter API and covers the three main formats and sharding styles in Inventory.
- End-to-end integration tests pass and show non-regression for correctness.
- Benchmarks show <= 10% increase in cold-start wall time and >= 15% reduction in peak memory for at least 70% of models in sample set when lazy activation is enabled.

Open questions:
- Should segment-mapper export a compact manifest format that becomes the canonical input for Dedicated/Private deployment artifact registries? (Product asks yes, but needs registry changes)
- Do we provide an optional on-disk canonicalization utility (transform checkpoint -> canonical segmented blob) as a migration tool? (adds operational cost but simplifies runtime)

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Segment+ Mapper+Design
- PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- Perf harness baseline runs: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/bench/model-bootstrap/2025-02
